records.issue_text: [Critical/security] The database default `1` maps to `raw_html`, not `regular`, causing new and migrated posts to bypass cooking/sanitization, enabling stored XSS and breaking Markdown rendering.
records.rationale: The finding claims default `1` maps to `raw_html`. The diff's `def self.cook_methods; Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html)` mirrors the existing `def self.types; Enum.new(:regular, :moderator_action)` pattern (Discourse's Enum assigns 1 to the first symbol), so `Post.cook_methods[:regular] == 1` and the migration's `default: 1` correctly maps to `regular`, not `raw_html`. The parallel with the existing types enum contradicts the claimed mapping.

records.issue_text: [High/security] Feed/imported HTML is stored as `raw_html` and rendered with `raw post.cooked`, while `CGI.unescapeHTML`/`scrub` does not sanitize it, allowing malicious feeds or source pages to persist scripts or event handlers into forum pages.
records.rationale: The diff confirms the mechanism: TopicEmbed.import creates posts with cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html], Post#cook then returns raw unsanitized, and app/views/embed/best.html.erb renders <%= raw post.cooked %>. Content comes from remote RSS (SimpleRSS.parse open(...)) or readability extraction with only CGI.unescapeHTML/scrub applied — no HTML sanitization anywhere in the diff — so scripts/handlers from a malicious feed or source page persist into pages served to browsers. Verified from the diff.

records.issue_text: [High/security] `open(url).read` follows redirects after validating only the original embed URL host, allowing an approved host to redirect requests to internal services (SSRF) and potentially publish internal response content.
